description: The title Candace, derived from the Meroitic Kandake, referred to powerful royal women of the Kingdom of Kush rather than to a single queen. Kandakes could serve as queen mothers, regents, or ruling monarchs in their own right, and several appear in ancient sources as politically and militarily active figures. The most famous, Amanirenas, led Kushite resistance against Roman expansion in the late 1st century BC, helping establish the Kandake as an enduring symbol of female sovereignty, dynastic authority, and martial leadership in ancient Nubia.
